bullets.text: At least six people were killed in Krakow, Poland, by a gunman in military fatigues who opened fire in the city.
Kenya's doomsday sect leader Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in jail for the murder of 190 children and one adult, after ordering his followers to starve themselves and their families.
New Zealand's general election resulted in no clear winner, with preliminary results indicating a highly divided national parliament, likely leading to weeks of coalition talks.

A leading forensic psychiatrist has criticised Corrections NSW, stating it should not manage mental health care for inmates, following an ABC investigation into systemic failures in the treatment of prisoners with mental illness.
The latest interest rate rise is setting in, shifting attention from the Melbourne Cup to household finances, as the race to tame inflation proves more challenging.
The city of Sydney is experiencing its annual 'purple patch' as jacaranda trees bloom across the area, creating picturesque scenes in October and November.

Berkshire Hathaway increased its share buybacks, purchasing $9.6 billion in stock during the third quarter, even as its operating income declined by 5.8 percent year-on-year due to an insurance slowdown.
Investors are concerned that Democratic dominance in Congress will hinder the growth of the AI sector, a sentiment reflected in market reactions to the US midterms.
Turkish authorities have detained top officials from the country's regulatory bodies as part of an expanding fund scandal investigation.
